concept.name: Hierarchical clustering
concept.definition: A family of clustering methods that creates a nested tree of groups by successively merging clusters or splitting them according to a linkage criterion.
concept.intuition: It is a learnable mapping or representation used to turn features into predictions or groups.
concept.mechanics: Start with individual observations for agglomeration, repeatedly merge the closest pair under the linkage rule, and cut the resulting dendrogram at a chosen level.
concept.failure_modes: Flexible models can fit noise, shift under new regimes, and conceal instability when tuning is repeated on the same validation data.
concept.misconceptions: Greater model complexity or in-sample accuracy does not by itself imply better out-of-sample trading results.
concept.example: Ten assets begin as singletons; average-linkage merges them until a dendrogram cut yields three clusters.
